title: Counting with range()
description: A for loop that prints each value produced by range().

original.hint: Think about what range(1, 4) produces — what is the first value, and when does it stop?
walkthrough: range(1, 4) produces a sequence — it starts at the first argument and stops before the second.
On the first iteration, i is assigned the first value from that sequence.
print(i) outputs whatever i currently holds.
This repeats for each remaining value in the sequence.
When the sequence is exhausted, the loop ends.

mutation.diff_description: Applies an arithmetic expression to i before printing.
mutation.hint: The loop still runs the same number of times. What changes is how each value of i is transformed before being printed.
walkthrough: range(1, 4) still produces the same sequence as before.
On each iteration, the value printed is i with an arithmetic operation applied to it.
Trace what that operation does to each value of i in turn.

transfer.code:
total = 0
for n in range(1, 4):
    total = total + n
print(total)
transfer.hint: Instead of printing on each iteration, the loop is building up a value across iterations. What does total hold after each step?
walkthrough: total is initialised to 0 before the loop begins.
On each iteration, total is updated by adding the current value of n to it.
Trace the value of total after each iteration through the loop.
print(total) runs once, after the loop has finished — not inside it.
